name: LTX-23 Video Studio
tagline: Browser front end for LTX text-to-video and image-to-video generation, sold by the credit.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Credit packs and subscriptions are advertised but amounts were not confirmed.

verdictSummary: The visible product here is a prompt box, a settings panel, a queue, and a gallery, all of which an agent can produce before lunch. The part you are actually paying for is a GPU running a video diffusion model for several minutes per clip, plus whichever LTX checkpoints the operator has access to. Some LTX-Video weights are openly published, so a local build is not fantasy, but it needs a large consumer GPU and still lands behind the hosted versions on resolution, length, and synchronized audio. Point it at a hosted inference API instead and you have rebuilt the billing relationship with extra steps. This is a reseller wrapper, which makes it cheap to imitate and pointless to imitate.
coreLoopDIY: A local job queue and gallery that runs open LTX-Video weights on your own GPU from text or image prompts, with a saved prompt library.
requirements: NVIDIA GPU with at least 24GB VRAM, ideally more
Python with CUDA-enabled PyTorch and diffusers
Tens of gigabytes of disk for model weights
Patience: minutes of compute per short clip
whatYouLose: Access to the newest LTX checkpoints, which may never be published as open weights
Synchronized audio generation, which the open local pipelines mostly do not do
Someone else's fast GPUs, so a clip that takes 40 seconds hosted can take many minutes locally
Resolution and duration ceilings that are tuned by people who do this full time
Zero-setup use from a phone or a laptop with no GPU
moatNotes: The moat is rented, not owned: this is a storefront in front of someone else's models and someone else's GPUs, which means it is easy to clone and easy to be cloned.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because video inference is the rare AI task where the compute bill is obvious and unavoidable. A ten second clip is thousands of frames of denoising, and most people do not have a 4090 sitting idle, let alone the appetite to babysit CUDA versions and 40GB checkpoint downloads. Paying per credit converts a hardware problem into a line item, and for anyone generating a handful of clips a month that is straightforwardly the cheaper option. The front end is not worth money, the minutes are.
notes: The UI is an afternoon of work; the frames are not. The moat is GPU minutes and model checkpoints that someone else trained and someone else hosts.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user AI video generation workbench. Do not build accounts, billing, telemetry, or any cloud component.

Stack, no substitutions: Python 3.11, FastAPI backend, SQLite via sqlite3, plain HTML plus htmx plus vanilla CSS for the UI, diffusers plus PyTorch for inference, ffmpeg via subprocess for encoding.

Scope that is IN:
- A /generate form with: prompt, negative prompt, optional input image for image-to-video, width, height, number of frames, fps, guidance scale, seed, and steps.
- A single-worker background job queue (one asyncio task pulling from a SQLite jobs table, status: queued, running, done, failed). One job at a time, because one GPU.
- An inference module that loads an open LTX-Video pipeline from diffusers by model id read from MODEL_ID in .env, keeps it resident between jobs, and supports both text-to-video and image-to-video paths.
- Write frames to MP4 with ffmpeg, h264, yuv420p, at the requested fps. Store outputs under ./outputs/{job_id}.mp4 and record the full parameter set in SQLite.
- A gallery page: newest first, inline video preview, the exact params used, a "re-run with tweaks" button that prefills the form, and a delete button.
- A prompt library: a prompts table with title, body, tags; save any prompt from a job, insert any saved prompt into the form. Seed it with six cinematic example prompts.
- A /health endpoint reporting GPU name, free VRAM, and whether the pipeline is loaded.

Scope that is OUT: audio generation, upscaling, multi-GPU, user auth, model fine-tuning, and any hosted inference API fallback. If no CUDA device is present, fail loudly at startup with a clear message instead of silently falling back to CPU.

Config: MODEL_ID, OUTPUT_DIR, MAX_FRAMES, DEFAULT_STEPS in .env, loaded with python-dotenv. Ship .env.example, never a real .env.

Deliver: requirements.txt, a README with exact setup commands, the VRAM floor you are assuming, and a one-command run script. Add a seeded smoke test that enqueues a 25 frame job at low resolution and asserts an MP4 lands on disk.
